text:
maria-liu: seeing a spike of provisioning failures for the eu-west-1 GPU autoscale group starting ~1781023400. error shows 'access denied' when pulling sidecar image and when trying to decrypt instance volume with KMS. any idea if the recent egress lockdown rule rolled out?
aj: yes i rolled a tighter egress ACL this morning around 08:10 UTC to restrict artifact-registry access. i didn't expect KMS or ECR decryption to be affected but maybe metadata endpoints are blocked.
sanjay-ram: can you paste the failing log snippet?
maria-liu: here's the kubelet log from one failed node: ```Mar 17 08:24:12 kubelet[1234]: failed to pull image "gcr.io/redwood-sidecars/cache:stable": rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = access denied
Mar 17 08:24:13 kms-client: failed to decrypt volume key: AccessDeniedException: not authorized to use kms key arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456789:key/abcd-efgh```
karen-ops: pinging infra-bot for recent firewall rollout info @infra-bot :eyes:
infra-bot: rollout "egress-tighten-v2" applied to eu-west-1 on 1781023000 by aj. Affected security group sg-0a1b2c3d. Audit tag: rollout/egress-tighten-v2.
aj: ok that explains it. i keyed off known artifact domains but missed KMS and metadata endpoints. quick fix: allow outbound to `169.254.169.254` and `kms.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com` plus registry IPs.
maria-liu: can we do a narrow exception for the autoscale GPU subnet instead of opening cluster-wide? don't want to widen the blast radius.
sanjay-ram: propose adding a rule to the subnet's NACL/SG for the GPU nodes: allow TCP 443 to kms.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com and UDP/TCP to artifact registry ranges. i'll prepare the ACL change.
karen-ops: we should also add an IAM policy exception: nodes use instance profile `redwood-gpu-node` which may need kms:Decrypt on that key. aj can you confirm the key policy wasn't modified?
aj: i didn't touch the KMS key policy. looks like the key has a condition restricting usage to a set of VPC endpoints that got removed in the previous PR. PR #4528 reverted the VPC endpoint id list; that caused KMS calls from nodes to fail.
maria-liu: ugh. so two concurrent things: egress rule tightened and key policy condition narrowed. that explains the simultaneous failures.
sanjay-ram: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily open egress to kms and metadata for GPU subnet (karen to execute), 2) rollback PR #4528 or update key policy to include node role (aj to coordinate with security), 3) add targeted rule in next deploy to avoid broad egress, 4) add automated test for node KMS access in canary provisioning. estimate 20min to mitigate.
karen-ops: I'm on it, executing NACL change for subnet s-0abc... now. patching ingress/outbound rules, will monitor.
infra-bot: change applied: NACL s-0abc updated at 1781023600 by karen-ops.
maria-liu: provisioning retries succeeding on 3/5 nodes now, still failing on 2 with the KMS error.
aj: opening a rollback on PR #4528 now, tagging security @sanjay-ram.
sanjay-ram: approved rollback. also filing a follow-up ticket TKT-8891 to add unit test in infra-provisioner that attempts a `kms:Decrypt` with node profile during canary.
karen-ops: note for runbook — add an entry about 'egress tighten' checklist: list of dependent services (ECR/GCR, KMS endpoints, metadata) and quick revert commands. i'll create runbook page. https://redwood.internal/runbooks/egress-tighten (draft).
maria-liu: once stable, let's run a short postmortem: root cause was config overlap: key policy condition + aggressive ACL. could be automation ordering issue.
aj: agreed. will coordinate a staged rollout with a smoke-provisioning job before blanket apply.
sanjay-ram: also adding audit-logs: we should make sure CloudTrail flagged these KMS AccessDenied events and attach them to the incident. ticket INC-3247.
karen-ops: all green now, autoscale finished 10 new nodes, no more provisioning failures. closing mitigation. follow-ups assigned: aj (policy fix), sanjay-ram (canary test), karen-ops (runbook), maria-liu (postmortem).
maria-liu: thanks everyone :thumbsup: keep updates in this thread if anything else pops up.
